articles.title: Digital levy: While Germany waits, big tech’s tax gap grows

Last year, Culture and Media Minister Wolfram Weimer promised a key-points paper on digital levies leading to a draft law. The paper has yet to appear. – Alle Rechte vorbehalten: photothek Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft and Netflix dominate the global digital infrastructure. The so-called Silicon Six are earning jaw-dropping profits, but the share they pay in taxes keeps shrinking. At the same time, the tax gap is widening. This is the amount countries would have collected in taxes if profits had been taxed in the countries where they were earned. The Fair Tax Foundation , a British NGO, puts the gap over the last decade at €278 billion ($316.7 billion). A third of that is in Europe alone. Taxed like a tax haven The Silicon Six’s profits have skyrocketed in the last decade, and their market value shows it.
